data.what_pass_means: the signed D3'-R plan (at the final resizing s), emulated with the S1 proxy at clean fraction 0.7 f, converges: the last doubling of shots moves E_R(B_sig) by less than the energy error H1's recall target tolerates, the Weinstein certificate meets H1 (0.1, B=0) / H2 (0.15, B=1) already at N/2 and brackets E0, the equal-shots Krylov curve is flat from k = 3 to 4 within E_tol, the device basis beats random bases of its size by >= E_tol, and B_sig carries >= 0.99 of the ground-state weight -- in all three seeds, both sectors, f = 0.05 / 0.10 / 0.15.  It is an emulation of the plan, not a device statement

stop.rule: prompts/30 section 10: STOP (planner returns) if CV3 fails at any f in any sector (family question: k = 5 is an owner signature, amendment 01 item 3) or if re-sizing to s = 8 still fails

notes.three_seeds: three seeds cannot establish the 95 % probability of the D3'-R rule; the conservative reading (every one of the three seeds must pass) is used
notes.width_no_plateau: no plateau constant is imposed on the certificate width: the Weinstein certificate is rigorous for any B, it must meet the H1/H2 target, and shrinking further with shots is not a requirement of H1/H2
notes.B_sig_nesting: the prefixes nest B_all and the counts exactly; B_sig is NOT nested by construction, because its threshold mu_s = N a / dim rises with N (a state with the same count at a larger N can fall below the one-sided 3 sigma level).  CV0 therefore checks nesting and monotonicity on B_all and on the counts, and reports the number of B_sig non-nested steps as information
notes.gap_B1: at B=1 gap_assumption_holds is expected false (near-degenerate cluster, splitting 0.024, manual 1.5); the rigorous statement is 'some eigenvalue in [E_R - r_H, E_R + r_H]' (manual 5.3)
notes.random_baseline_solver: random baselines: lowest eigenpair of the sparse projected block by Lanczos (scipy eigsh, tol 1e-12), agreeing with the dense eigh to ~3e-14; device bases: skqd.skqd.ritz
notes.cv4_points: CV4 is evaluated at every shots-curve point phi = 1/16..1 and every equal-shots k = 1..4 (the criterion curves), plus the N/2 and N points of a re-sized plan; the allocation and 2 N_c curves are information
notes.cause_of_failure: CV2 and CV3 fail on the WIDTH condition (r_H <= 0.1 at B=0, 0.15 at B=1) on B_sig; CV1, CV4, CV5 and CV0 hold everywhere.  The ladder table shows why re-sizing cannot rescue B=0: B_sig keeps a state only when its count is one-sided 3 sigma above mu_s = N a / dim, and mu_s grows linearly with N, so the count a state needs to enter B_sig rises with every doubling (2 counts at the 1x plan, 4-5 at 8x), and the low-weight neighbours that set r_H stay out; on B_all the same samples meet the width at 8x (column 'max r_H(sN/2) B_all').  CV3 fails on the width at every cell and, at B=1, also on the energy plateau in several seeds; on the 2 N_c curve the k plateau holds in most seeds while the width does not (table 'CV3 on the 2 N_c curve').  The re-run of the chunks on the plan read from validation/Q0P_2x3_plan.json (same samples, cache) reproduced every value: a second failure under the retry rule, so the gate is BLOCKED and the planner returns.  No constant, tolerance, the P9 rule or the signed family was changed
notes.resize_floor: re-sized floor circuits get ceil100(267 s) shots; at s = 8 that is 2,200 > the 8 x 267 = 2,136 sampled, so those circuits are evaluated at 2,136 (fewer shots: conservative) and listed
